news.title: FBI Impersonation Scams Hit 61,000 Victims — $1.6 Billion Lost
news.excerpt:
The FBI says scammers impersonating government officials have hit nearly 61,000 people since January 2025, stealing over $1.6 billion. They call or email pretending to be the FBI, IRS, Social Security, or local police — saying you owe money, your identity was stolen, or there's a warrant. They demand payment by wire, gift card, or crypto.

What to do: Hang up. Government agencies never call demanding money or threatening arrest. If you're worried, look up the real number yourself and call back.…

news.title: Hurricane Charity Scams Are Targeting Floridians — Here's How to Spot Them
news.excerpt: Hurricane season runs through November, and scammers know it. After every storm, fake charity websites, crowdfunding campaigns, and phone calls flood in — all pretending to help victims. They'll pressure you to donate right now. They'll ask for gift cards, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency. Real charities never ask for those. They'll use names that sound almost like real organizations (e.g., "Florida Hurricane Relief Fund" vs. the real "Florida Disaster Fund"). What to do: Before donating, verify the charity at ftc.gov/charity or guidestar.org. Pay by credit card only — it has fraud protection. If someone calls pushing for immediate payment, hang up.

posts.truth: Most people think "I don't have enterprise gear, this doesn't apply to me." But if your router runs on any of these platforms — or your IT provider uses them — you're exposed. I've seen small businesses get hit because their managed service provider hadn't patched a VPN gateway in months.

posts.title: Your free Columbia County library card unlocks the Libby app for free e-books and audiobooks
posts.summary: Visit any Columbia County library branch (Main Library at 308 NW Columbia Ave in Lake City, Fort White Branch, or West Branch) with a photo ID and proof of address. Get a free library card, then access the Libby app for free e-books and audiobooks on your phone or tablet, Career Online High School for a free accredited high school diploma, and the Florida Electronic Library databases for research. All free with your card.
posts.truth: Most people think the library is just for books. It's not — it's a tech support center you've already paid for with your taxes. I've sent customers there for help setting up email, learning video calls, and printing documents when their home printer dies.

posts.title: Stop fighting weird video formats — VLC Media Player is the free Swiss Army knife that plays literally everything
posts.summary: Download VLC free at videolan.org/vlc — choose "Windows 64-bit" for most computers. Install it, and it will play any video or audio file you throw at it: MKV, AVI, MP4, MOV, FLAC, MP3, DVDs, Blu-rays, network streams, even broken or incomplete downloads. No codec packs, no ads, no tracking, no subscriptions. Ever.
posts.truth: I've seen people pay for "video converter" software to make a file play in Windows Media Player. VLC plays the original file without converting. The only format it struggles with is DRM-protected commercial movies (iTunes, some streaming downloads) — and that's by design, not a bug.

posts.title: Windows can clean up your disk automatically — Storage Sense frees space while you sleep
posts.summary: Turn on Storage Sense at Settings > System > Storage. Flip the switch to On, then click "Storage Sense" to choose how often it runs (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or "When low on disk space") and what to clean: temporary files, Recycle Bin (after 30 days by default), and Downloads folder (if you want). It's free, built into Windows 10 and 11, and runs automatically in the background.
posts.truth: People buy "PC cleaner" software that does exactly what Storage Sense does for free — and the paid ones often delete things they shouldn't. Microsoft's built-in tool is conservative: it only removes files Windows knows are safe to delete.

posts.title: Stop paying for Microsoft Office — LibreOffice 25.2 is free, opens every file, and now has themes
posts.summary: LibreOffice 25.2 is free at libreoffice.org. Download the Windows 64-bit installer, run it, and you can open Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files without paying Microsoft a dime. New in 25.2: built-in themes (Light, Dark, and custom colors) so you can make it look exactly how you want — go to Tools > Options > Appearance to pick one.
posts.truth: I see people paying $70–$100 a year for Office 365 just to open a few documents. LibreOffice has opened every Office file I've thrown at it for 15 years. The only time it struggles is with heavily macro-laden Excel sheets — and most people don't use those.
